prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a downward-angled ground scene where the camera wearer's lower torso and yellow garment at the bottom are nearest (0.2–0.4 m, brightest white), outstretched hands holding knitting needles sit just above and in front at 0.4–0.6 m, a mint-green knitted cloth and yarn ball rest on a plastic sheet on the ground at 0.7–1.0 m, and a second seated person in yellow and blue jeans is to the upper right at roughly 0.8–1.3 m (about 0.3–0.6 m from the knitted cloth). The camera wearer faces downward toward their hands and the ground, while the second person's legs and torso are angled toward the left and bottom-left without their head entering the frame to show if they look at the camera wearer; the needles, yarn ball, and cloth are within arm's reach of both people, while red flip-flops on the ground to the left sit just at the edge of the camera wearer's reach (0.8–1.1 m). Across the five frames, the second person leans forward and downward into the right foreground in frame 2 (brightening to about 0.5–0.7 m and partially occluding the plastic sheet) before retreating toward the upper right in frames 3–5 as the camera view shifts slightly upward and right, while both people's upper bodies and heads remain cropped out of view at the bottom and top-right edges. Compared to the RGB strip, the depth map makes the 3D relief of the crumpled clothfolds, the elevated height of the wearer's hands and needles above the ground, and the sudden forward lean of the second person in frame 2 much easier to judge. However, the map is unreliable along the right edge in frames 2–5 where cast shadows and ground textures create a smooth, artificially bright foreground ramp, and thin knitting needles and yarn strands vanish in frames 4–5.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map attempts to isolate foreground figures and items on the ground plane, where in the RGB context the camera wearer's torso and arms occupy the bottom foreground (0.2–0.6 m), a pile of mint-green knitting and red flip-flops lie in the middle ground (0.7–1.1 m, left to center), and another seated person is positioned to the upper right (0.8–1.3 m, about 0.5 m from the wearer's hands). The camera wearer faces forward and down toward the objects within arm's reach (yarn, needles, and cloth), while the second person sits to the right facing left/downward with their head out of frame and their hands within reach of the cloth and their own knees. Across the five frames, the pink 'person' mask captures the camera wearer's hands, torso, and the adjacent red flip-flop in frame 1, expands in frame 2 to merge the wearer with the green knitted cloth as the second person leans in on the right, shifts in frame 3 to cover the green cloth and part of the wearer's torso while omitting the right arm, and disappears entirely in frame 4 before frame 5 mislabels the upper-right seated person and cloth as 'teddy bear' masks in blue and light green. While the masks roughly indicate the contiguous footprint of the foreground figures and cloth pile against the bare ground in the first three frames, they provide almost no spatial detail that is clearer than RGB. The map is highly unreliable throughout, failing to separate the two individuals or the green textile from the wearer's body, missing the second person completely in frames 1–4, dropping all detections in frame 4, and hallucinating 'teddy bear' labels over both people and the background ground in frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map tracks the 2D skeletal keypoints of the camera wearer's left and right hands (magenta) located in the lower-central foreground at roughly 0.4–0.6 m from the viewpoint, hovering above the ground plane within immediate arm's reach of the knitting needles and yarn ball, while the second person seated 0.8–1.3 m away to the upper right is never detected. In all frames, the camera wearer's body is below the bottom edge facing downward toward the hands, and across frames 1 to 5 the two magenta hand skeletons change orientation and separation—tilting inward along the knitting needles in frame 1, losing the left hand detection in frame 2 while the right hand stays at the center-right, moving close together near the center in frame 3 as the left hand grasps the needle tip, and spreading apart again in frames 4 and 5 as the left hand reaches toward the yarn ball on the left and drops to the lower left. Although the second person leans into the right side of frame 2 and sits with visible arms and legs in the upper right of frames 3–5 (within arm's reach of the cloth pile and roughly 0.5–0.8 m from the wearer's hands), their body and hands remain completely unmapped, and their head stays cropped out of view so gaze toward the wearer cannot be confirmed. The pose map makes it easier than RGB alone to see the exact finger articulation and pinch posture of the camera wearer's hands against the similarly toned ground and clutter across time. However, it is unreliable where it drops the camera wearer's left hand in frame 2, hallucinates a distorted yellow upper-body skeleton over the green knitted cloth in frame 3, and fails to detect any body or hand keypoints for the second person in the upper right across all five frames.
